title: Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
authors: Yingxi Bai, Zihan Chen, Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang
abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.
summary: This work establishes ferroelastic switching as a powerful, non-volatile control mechanism for manipulating the magnon thermal Hall effect in fully compensated ferrimagnets. By exploiting symmetry changes, the authors show that the transverse heat transport can be reversed without altering the net magnetization. This mechanism is predicted to be realized in materials like monolayer V2SSe, opening avenues for advanced magnonic devices.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving reversible and nonvolatile control over the magnon thermal Hall response in magnetic systems that possess zero net magnetization.
main_result: The study demonstrates that ferroelastic switching can reverse the sign of the magnon thermal Hall effect ($\kappa_{xy}$) in fully compensated ferrimagnets while maintaining zero net magnetization.
method: The research combines theoretical modeling using a Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Hamiltonian with first-principles calculations (Green's function, NEB) to predict material behavior.
model_or_system: The system under study is a fully compensated ferrimagnet, exemplified by monolayer V2SSe. The theoretical framework involves a minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model applied to a 2D lattice, incorporating ferroelastic switching as the control mechanism.
key_observables: Magnon Thermal Hall Conductivity ($\kappa_{xy}^M$), Orbital Hall Conductivity ($\sigma_{Lz}$), and Magneto-optical spectra (Kerr/Faraday).
important_parameters: The control mechanism relies on the symmetry operation [C2 || C4z] relating two orthogonal ferrimagnetic variants.
main_assumptions: Model calculations often assume $A_z = 0$, and thermal Hall calculations are limited to temperatures below 200 K.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Heisenberg-DM model, the temperature dependence of $\kappa_{xy}$ across different magnetic phases, chirality-resolved band structures, and the evolution of magnetic configuration during ferroelastic switching.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using a minimal Hamiltonian, analyzes the effect of ferroelastic switching on magnon bands and Berry curvature, and validates the findings using first-principles calculations on a candidate material, V2SSe.
why_interesting: The ability to non-volatilely switch a topological response (like the thermal Hall effect) using a structural/lattice degree of freedom (ferroelasticity) is highly relevant for developing next-generation spintronic and magnonics devices.

FIG. 2. Schematic illustration of the magnetic-configuration evolu- tion and accompanying spin-group symmetry reconstruction during ferroelastic switching. The two fFIM states are mapped onto each other by spin-space operation [C2 ∥C4z], and the corresponding spin groups are indicated below each configuration. Red and blue blocks denote opposite spin sublattices. Here, C2 denotes a twofold spin rotation about an axis perpendicular to the spin axis, H denotes a halving subgroup of the crystallographic Laue group, A denotes a real-space rotation or mirror operation (C or M).
